item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 14
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 14 twice. This episode was the last episode of the first part of season 3.

So, obviously, the diary shocked him deeply. He was crying, throwing up, and he even vividly understood how Sylphie would die. Maybe the future him added every single detail about her death in the diary so he could remember. So, after that moment, he did everything, even every little thing, kindly because he had seen the horrible things the future him did to everyone. But obviously, that wasn't how he usually acted, so other people thought something was wrong with him and worried about him. Aisha, especially, prepared meals more than usual, for instance.

I wondered what Rudy would do, but he figured out he was able to prevent Roxy from getting the disease. So, he just shared a few things, not all, with Sylphie and Roxy. He couldn't tell them about Man God or about his future self, so he only told them fragments of the facts. The biggest one was that he was going to marry Eris, and Sylphie worried about him because she knew how badly Rudy had been hurt by her. So she was against it. But Roxy didn't know about that time or who Eris was, so she instead suggested meeting Eris and figuring it out.

Then Man God came and this time it confessed a few things. It couldn't foresee that the future Rudy would come. It was able to see multiple possible futures and interfere, but some people's destinies were too strong. Rudy and his family were among them, but Man God figured out his unborn babies didn't have them and had a chance to kill them. Interesting. So that was how it was. And then Orsted was the only one who could kill Man God, but he couldn't reach it because he was alone. Man God was going to be killed by Orsted and descendants of Rudy, and that was the reason it interfered with Rudy. Anyway, Rudy was ready to accept whatever Man God asked and Man God asked him to kill Orsted. And that was what he made up his mind to do. Honestly, I hadn't understood why he obeyed Man God, but obviously, it was the suggestion of the future him. He has to doubt Man God but must not antagonize it, to avoid putting his family at risk. Anyhow, he made up his mind to kill a person, and Sylphie and Roxy were so confused. I get them. This didn't totally make sense because the previous night, he had shared secrets with them, but when he got up, he was suddenly grave and said something you didn't want to do. Couldn't Roxy notice something, considering how long she has lived?

Also, I kinda expected it, but Man God said the future Rudy had misunderstood things. I think he pinned every failure on Man God, like Luke's or anything else, so I wondered which ones weren't actually caused by Man God and which ones were. I think Luke's was actually caused by Man God, but I don't know about the other things, like Zanoba's and Aisha's cases, for example.

Anyhow, of the three things the future him recommended, he started by writing a letter to Eris. On the other hand, Eris was about to leave the Sword Sanctuary. She talked with Nina about some facts and groundless rumors about Rudy. One said, for instance, he was a womanizer who didn't sleep with the same woman more than twice. Was that the gossip about a man who was already married to two women?! Anyhow, at that time, she received Rudy's letter. She couldn't even figure out how to open it so she used the sword. How bad she was at everything except the sword! Then she couldn't read some of the words, so Isolde, the Water King, read the letter. The letter told her how he had felt when Eris left him, and he was already married to two wives, so she was going to be the 3rd wife. Of course, she was shocked and her mind went blank, and also Isolde got mad because she felt Rudy didn't respect women and even asked Eris to come to Asura. But at the end, he also shared he was going to challenge Orsted and might lose his life. At that moment, she decided to go to him either way and left. I hadn't noticed, but now Eris's purpose, fighting Orsted, had become the same as Rudy's. And this scene was very good. That also proved that Eris' training was actually right on the money.

So, this was the end of part 1 of season 3. Honestly, this entire part was mostly just preparation for the next. Still, episode 13 was extremely good, depressing, and cruel, so it was worth watching. It was one of the best episodes I've ever watched, and obviously one of the three best episodes this year. It was especially amazing because we knew what was going to happen, but it went over the high bar the previous episode set. Also, we learned a little about Man God, so this was actually a pretty important part so far.

On top of that, I liked Zanoba, Cliff, and Nanahoshi more because they joined and moved with Rudy more in this part. In part 2, I hope things move more.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Rudeus: 6/10
    • Well, I kinda understood why he didn't, but still I wanted him to share the secrets with his wives at least.
    • I didn't fully understand why he tried to fight Orsted. He shouldn't antagonize Man God, but does he still have to do whatever Man God asks now?
  • Sylphie: 7/10
    • She rarely showed her anxiety about Rudy. Sometimes, she should put her feelings first. It was so weird that Rudy didn't share more of his secrets.
  • Roxy: 8/10
    • She was, like a wife but always saw things objectively. Maybe because she was the second wife? Or simply because she has lived so long?
  • Eris: 6/10
    • Honestly, I felt a little sorry for her when Rudy's letter was read. From her point of view, she didn't do anything wrong.
  • Isolde: 8/10
    • I liked that she despised Rudy from a short letter and even asked Eris to come to Asura. She was a nice person
  • Man God: 2/10
    • I now understand why it tried to interfere with Rudy's life.
    • But I didn't believe for a second that its objective was world peace after watching the previous episode.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 13
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 13 twice.

This episode was all about what happened to the future Rudy who showed up in the previous episode. In the previous episode, there were no flashback scenes, just the two Rudies talking to each other, but in this episode, we were able to see what actually happened to the future Rudy. This was depressing and heartbreaking.

So, as expected, first Roxy got the petrification after a few cats or rats had been seen. And Cliff was the first to figure it out, and he also found out how and where to cure it. So Rudy, Cliff, and Zanoba went to the Millis church to get the sacred text. I thought they would get the god-class detoxification magic the official way, but they stole it! That was something unexpected. And of course they were chased, and on the way, Cliff got hurt and died. In the last episode, I wondered when he had died, but he died even before Roxy did. And he belonged to the Millis religion, but he even stole its bible to prioritize saving Roxy. I liked Cliff even more here, but I got sad when he died. Of course, Elinalise got mad at Rudy and hit him, but he was well aware that she had the right to do it. Anyway, Roxy was already dead when Rudy went back to his home.

Then Sylphie was trying to comfort him, but he couldn't recover from his depression. Without someone's help, he couldn't do it at all. And then, because he was depressed, he stopped by a brothel one night, but the next morning, Sylphie found him at the door. The future Rudy didn't mention this at all, probably because it was too pathetic for him to talk about. I guess she was worried about him and went looking for him, but it came back to haunt her. Anyhow, that was how she left him and joined the rebels in the Asura Kingdom. Rudy was still a complete mess, but when Rudy's mother slapped him, he decided to follow Sylphie and bring her back. But when he arrived at the Asura capital, all the rebels were dead, and Rudy saw all of them, including Sylphie, crucified. And I didn't notice at first, but she had lost her right arm too. And when he saw her, he flew into a rage and burned an entire kingdom completely. At this point, he was a real terrorist attacking Millis and Asura. The scene was cruel and depressing, but here, he crossed the line completely. He was emotional but I didn't expect he could do this.

After that, his life got even more messed up, and even Lilia gave up on fixing him and all of them left his mansion. He still went to the academy and built a robot that looked like Sylphie. He couldn't build Roxy? Probably he wanted to apologize and really wanted to make things right with Sylphie, so he tried to make her first, but it looked fragile. Anyhow, when I saw that, Zanoba and Julie built some really cool stuff, like an android. But it seemed he broke it by himself? Maybe he didn't want to see a fake her and insult her. He also helped Nanahoshi as he did before. However, Nanahoshi killed herself while he wasn't there. I was expecting him to be there for the last experiment, but he wasn't. It was such a regrettable thing.

But then, years later, Aisha came back to his mansion as an adult and helped him as a maid. She really loved her brother. So he wondered why he couldn't pull himself together after Roxy's death.

Then, he dreamed of Man God. And it told him that the displacement incident had changed the future. And Man God couldn't affect him, so it needed to gain his trust and eliminate Roxy. Once he heard that, he decided to find Man God and started searching the world. He met Eris and Ghislaine from time to time: when he was trying to save Roxy, when he went to Sylphie, and at other times. But she kept attacking him, and he was trying to get information about Man God even from her but of course he couldn't. He didn't really have any clue at that time. Then he didn't want to take the risk of talking to Perugius in case he was connected with Man God, so he decided to get information from Atofe. I don't understand why they started fighting. I guess he just turned down what Atofe said. Anyway, he couldn't defeat her. And then Eris saved him and was killed. At this point, at least 30 years had passed, and Eris and Ghislaine still followed him. She really couldn't find the right words to tell him, and kept loving him for more than three decades. During those years, Rudy couldn't think about much else because he was always occupied with the deaths of Roxy and Sylphie, and then with Man God. So there was no room in his mind for Eris.

Right before he fought against Atofe, his mansion was also attacked somehow, and Zanoba, Julie, and Aisha were killed too. It was still unclear why, but it seemed one of the kingdoms had attacked his mansion. Anyway, he apparently destroyed that kingdom for vengeance. So, at this point, he lost almost all of his family and friends. What it didn't show was what happened to Lilia, his mother, Norn, Elinalise, Sara, and demon's princesses. The rest of them died before they got old.

Then somehow, he found a place with a dragon mural, and he understood that the world had been made by combining six worlds. And Man God was in the center of those worlds, which basically had nothing. What were the six worlds? Demon world, human world, and what else? Or, maybe each God Style actually comes from a different world? Sword, North, Water, Dragon, and what else? Anyhow, he figured out 5 world items were required but needed a decade for each item, and he wouldn't live for that long. So, he got so strong and even cured his own arm with his magic, but he couldn't stop his aging with magic, unfortunately. And he decided to teleport himself into the past and he actually made it, as we saw in the last episode. In his last moment, he saw Sylphie and Roxy, and he saw them with his right eye, which can see the future. That didn't happen in the last episode, so he was able to see further into the future than current Rudy can, I guess.

Anyhow, since he came back to the past with teleportation magic, could that help Nanahoshi's experiment and make her magic successful? I wonder if Rudy will tell her about his future self. Also, Man God can influence many others, apparently, so that was the reason why the future Rudy told current Rudy that he shouldn't rely too much on others, because Man God can interfere. I guess Nanahoshi won't get affected, though. Demons like Roxy probably won't either. Then what will the world items be? I think collecting them and figuring out that dragon board (mural?) will be Rudy's goal. Also, what did Man God mean by "the future changed"? This guy obviously knows many scenarios of the future and also how to make them happen, so how could he not notice? Merging another world?

Music was good. At first, it was bright, but in a sad, depressing moment, the music stopped completely. Throughout this episode, the BGM was depressing or sad. Also, voice performance was pretty good in this episode. I liked Sylphie's voice performance in each scene, and also Man God when it laughed at Rudy and enjoyed it viciously.

Anyhow, will Rudy contact Eris, ask Nanahoshi for help, or maybe try to stop the civil war in the Asura Kingdom? I don't know what will come.

Scores

  • Episode: 10/10
  • Rudeus: 3/10
    • Well, I know he was depressed, but I kinda rated him lower in this episode. But I guess he is a normal person who can get devastated and can be even evil if the worst thing happens
  • Eris: 9/10
    • She had faith in him for decades. Okay, I really liked these kinds of characters.
  • Ghislaine: 10/10
    • This woman protected and served Eris for all those years and even saved Rudy. Cool.
  • Cliff: 9/10
    • I like a person who puts his friends before his own beliefs
  • Aisha: 8/10
    • Even Lilia, who had been grateful to him since she gave birth to Aisha, gave up on Rudy, but Aisha believed he would get back on his feet, and she came back.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 12
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 12 twice.

So, this episode was almost entirely about the talk between the current and future Rudy. What happened to the future Rudy was pretty horrible. First, Roxy died. I had wondered what would have happened if Rudy had gone to the basement. There was a rat in the basement, and the rat gave her the illness that killed her. I didn't expect that a little thing would kill somebody, but it was actually similar to Nanahoshi's mana illness. Also, Roxy had a baby in her belly and that caused it. So, it sounded like Man God wanted to kill Roxy or her baby, though old Rudy couldn't figure out its intent.

Next, Sylphie died. Because she couldn't get Rudy back on his feet after Roxy's death, she left to join the civil war in the Asura Kingdom and died. Luke was also tricked by Man God. So, not only Rudy but also other people were manipulated by it.

Then he fought against Eris again and again, and she died too. Nanahoshi's experiment also failed, and she died. It sounded like Cliff wasn't alive, but I don't know when he died. So overall, his life at the end was full of regret, after a few weeks of the same time in this episode. And that might've been the reason why he said he wasn't Rudy.

I also thought old Rudy knew who Man God was, but even he didn't know. At least he was named as Human God and now Man God, and also he said Man God couldn't be defeated. It was so convincing because he could even use a lot of strong magic like time travel, flying, or telepathy and still couldn't find it. Will the Rudy in this world win against it? I don't know. But as old Rudy said, Man God is the last boss, so he might be able to. But because of the time travel, old Rudy lost part of his body, and he was also near his end. But right before he died, he sensed Roxy and Sylphie over the wall, meaning he was also able to see things through obstacles like walls.

Rudy went out of the room and talked to them, but of course, he couldn't tell them what had really happened. He actually also followed what old Rudy said, because he said he shouldn't rely too much on others. I felt it was weird, but he lived by himself for a long time, so that might be the reason he said so. Anyhow, Roxy accepted that there was something he couldn't tell her, and they just went back to their rooms and decided not to leave their rooms that night. And Rudy just burned old Rudy's body and buried his bones in the ground. Then he decided to go to the basement and used ice magic before going in. And he found a frozen mouse with teeth made of petrified mana in the basement, as old Rudy guessed. Old Rudy also gave the diary to Rudy, and that's for the next episode.

So the next episode is probably what happened to the old Rudy, and it's going to be a horrible thing, I believe.

Scores

  • Episode: 8/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • It was great to see both old Rudy, who was full of regret, and Rudy, who saw that man and made up his mind that he didn't want to be like him.
  • Roxy: 8/10
    • She is an understanding girl. When Rudy can't tell her something, she accepts it without complaining.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 11
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 11 twice.

Because Rudy had a nightmare about Atofe, I thought Atofe would become another trauma for Rudy, but it seems not.

Nanahoshi got completely better. She needs to drink tea made from sokas grass every day to keep her illness away, but anyway, she got better and she was really grateful to Rudy. She had slapped him last time, but he forgave her anyway, and she even started showing him respect for the first time. They got along even better, and she wondered what his previous life was like, but he didn't want to talk about it. Well, he was nothing like the current Rudy back then, so it totally makes sense.

Then Cliff got a reward from Kishirika: a right eye like Rudy's, but its ability is to see all kinds of information about each person. He didn't say what kinds of information, but can he see whether Rudy was reincarnated from another world? I don't know. Maybe that wasn't a big issue either way.

Then Perugius started to like Rudy. He really hated demons, and the blow he dealt Atofe in the last episode was so good for him without him risking anything. Because he was able to get a chance to do so thanks to Rudy and Zanoba, he came to like them. I hadn't noticed that he didn't rely on or trust Rudy that much before, though. Maybe because his magic seemed like Laplace's? Zanoba also talked with Perugius a lot, and he also knew Ruijerd had saved Perugius before. Rudy was impressed when Zanoba talked about it, and it seemed he had forgotten it, so he tried to bring Ruijerd up with Perugius. Anyway, as a reward for dealing with Atofe, he got something from Perugius that he can use to call him. And I thought Princess Ariel was just sitting there, but when she brought up that she could bring statues, Perugius wasn't really interested in it. And instead, he asked her a question and she couldn't answer. The question was "What is the quality of a king?" What was that answer? I recalled something from Ling Yao from Fullmetal Alchemist, and it sounded similar to what Rudy said.

Anyhow, Rudy went back to his home, and hugged Roxy as he promised. Husband and wife moment. Then he talked about what happened and then he wrote a diary, and then Man God came to his dream. I knew because the title of this episode was "Turning Point 4." Then he talked about what would've happened if he had followed what Man God said. And everyone, including Roxy and his father, would've been saved. This sounded terribly wrong. Without him, Roxy would've been dead for sure in the dungeon. There was no way Paul and the others could've defeated the hydra without her and Rudy. So, they would probably all have died, or at least some of them would have. Anyway, Man God asked Rudy for a favor this time, which sounded pretty small. Because Rudy has a high EQ and felt sorry for Man God, he wanted to do what Man God said. At the end, Man God showed a creepy, vile smile in the animation, but it could still be just a misleading scene. Anyhow, Rudy was trying to go to his sanctuary in order to find something unusual, as Man God had told him. But then, an old guy came into the room out of the blue and told Rudy that he was from the future, proving it by saying Rudy's name from his previous life. I hadn't realized Rudy had never told anyone his name from his previous life, but now thinking about it, he only talked about the past life to Nanahoshi, and he didn't really want to talk about it, so there was no way anybody could know. And old Rudy said he had been deceived by Man God, but that was where the episode ended.

I don't know what will happen if he enters the basement. In the first place, what was the "something unusual"? And also, who is Man God? My guess is that Man God is actually Laplace, because that name has come up so many times so far. And Man God was actually sealed like Perugius said, so he was trying to come back to life. Also, that means just like he tricked Ruijerd's people, he was trying to trick Rudy. I don't know what the "something unusual" was. But maybe it could take over Rudy's body so that Man God could come back into the world. Then probably starting a war or something? Even if he wasn't Laplace, he sure was a legendary person like Orsted or Perugius and could cause a devastating result.

Anyway, what will the next episode be about? Old Rudy will talk about what will happen in the future, and Rudy will choose not to do that. But the title is "An End and a Beginning," so something big will start for sure.

Scores

  • Episode: 9/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • He kept his promise to Roxy.
    • He was also trying to do his best in this life
  • Zanoba: 8/10
    • Okay, I started liking him more and more. This guy is great
  • Perugius: 8/10
    • This guy might be legendary but this guy is definitely a person.
  • Man God: 4/10
    • He has been so suspicious, but in this episode, he kinda showed his true self for a moment.
    • At least he was a natural-born liar
    • Let's see how much of a scumbag this guy is.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 10
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 10 twice.

When Kishirika tried to surprise everybody by saying there was no sokas grass, they were about to get mad but tried not to show it. Their faces were so twisted, and it was funny. And of course, Cliff was the first to say it while Rudy was trying to hold it back. Then soldiers came and Moore spoke the human language instead of the demon tongue. I thought he was a human, but it seems I was wrong.

They went to the Demon King's tower, which was a good one, a tower with a spiral staircase. Rudy and Zanoba went to the throne to hand over Kishirika, while Cliff and Elinalise went to find the sokas grass. When Rudy met the Immortal Demon King, Atofe, she turned out to be a selfish and arrogant king who never listened to anyone. Kishirika actually warned them earlier so she was right. All the soldiers, Rudy, and Zanoba tried to stop her and were blown away. It looks like she was so strong, and she had lost only twice, to her husband Kalman, who was the North God, and to Laplace, so most of her soldiers were those people who couldn't flee from her. How sad they were. Anyhow, Moore allowed Rudy to leave with Kishirika.

But then Atofe was waiting for them in front of the warp gate. So, Rudy and Elinalise planned how to fight her, and decided to let Cliff leave the place and ask Perugius to help them. In the fight scene, and in this episode, Zanoba was so strong. Was he this strong all along? I didn't remember but he was so tough that even Atofe couldn't move. And it was interesting that the one Rudy couldn't stop wasn't Atofe, but Moore. He said he was a master of magic so he recognized how skillful he was. He used ice magic, quagmire, Disturb Magic, and even lightning, which even hurt his own side. But it couldn't completely stop them, but he was enough to stop.

Then, Perugius came to the place and used his magic on Atofe because it was a good chance for him. What happened to them? Was he angry with her or something? He knew it wouldn't kill her completely and he didn't intend to break the pact, so he wasn't serious. So, I didn't get what he was trying to do here.

Anyway, I feel like this fight can cause something bigger later. The next episode will be "Turning Point 4", so something big will happen in the next episode, or at least the next few episodes.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Rudeus: 7/10
    • In this episode, he showed a full range of expressions. He was frustrated, got scary, and was relieved.
  • Zanoba: 7/10
    • He is mature, mentally strong, and calm. How reliable he is.
    • And he is so tough and strong.
  • Kishirika: 5/10
    • Well, this is a kid.
    • It was interesting to see an animation of her right eye and it rotated to figure out who Rudeus was.
  • Perugius: 7/10
    • Did he hate the demon a lot?
  • Atofe: 5/10
    • She doesn't listen to whatever anyone else says. Stubborn woman. Also, she made others wait for 2 hours.
    • This king might be crazily strong in a fight scene, though
  • Moore: 4/10
    • What did he think? He gave Rudy some advice, but then he knew how it would turn out. I don't know what his aim was

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 18
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler, and not only about this episode.

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 18 twice.

The Volcanica Emilia faced was like an NPC in a game. It just kept repeating the same lines and tried to protect the pillar behind it. When Emilia got close to the pillar, she had to fight it. She used ice magic to create and summon her knights, and all of them are Subaru. She's a girl in love.

Subaru and Meili were fighting against Shaula's scorpion. And I wondered how he would fight it, but he was just trying to stop the scorpion, maybe unless it doesn't resist them? But the scorpion's attack shot Meili in the stomach. It seemed that Subaru would take on her damage with his new authority, Cor Leonis, but no such scene was animated.

The entire rest of this episode was about the fight between Ram and Gluttony. Subaru got his new authority, Cor Leonis, so he was able to take Ram's burden instead, and Ram was able to keep fighting against Gluttony. When did he remember this authority and how? There was no such scene. Maybe he learned it when the two of them merged, or while he was in the Corridor of Memories?

Anyhow, Ram was able to fight a lot longer than she used to. In the past, she lost her mana and stamina very quickly and couldn't fight for a long time at all. And knowing this, after fighting for a short period, Gluttony went to where Rem was, because he thought she couldn't catch up with him. But she was able to catch up with him and hit him. However, he was able to transform into Rem and she was blown away and then her rod was broken. But then, she realized that she and Rem shared everything, too. And it looks like the rod itself was actually made from her original horn? So, after that, she used Rem's power to fight him. She was originally a genius among the demons, so she overwhelmed him completely.

The fight scene between them was great. I wondered why they could fly so easily, but Ram can use her wind magic so she can fly and it made the fight interesting, especially on the huge spiral staircase in the tower. I didn't get what he drew on the wall at the end, but maybe it was love or something? Anyway, he got what he deserved. Because he pulled some memories from his body, does that mean many people's memories were back? Also, Ram's memories of Rem were coming back and her feelings toward Rem were coming back, too, even though it was not complete in this episode.

Also, I'd always wondered what Ram was thinking back when her horn was broken. Rem thought it was finally broken and was kinda relieved, and Rem blamed herself all along in her life for that relief. But Ram thought the same thing. Because Ram and Rem shared emotions and so on, as Ram explained in this episode, Ram might've also felt what Rem thought. Rem always thought and said Ram was the best, and Ram was proud of herself too, for example.

So, there are still 2 things remaining: Emilia's exam in the tower and Subaru fighting against the scorpion to break Shaula's curse. Will these be resolved? Also, will the memories of Julius and Emilia come back, and will Rem wake up? Those things should happen in the next episode.

Scores

  • Episode: 9/10
    • This episode is one of the best episodes for Ram. And also the episode for Ram and Rem. There was another best episode for her in season 2, but this episode also included her past.
  • Emilia: 8/10
    • She is a girl who loves Subaru. Her magic gets creative too.
  • Ram: 9/10
    • She was no longer the girl who gets wiped out after using magic, thanks to Subaru and Rem.
    • She defeated one of the Sin Archbishops by herself. Wasn't that a little too strong?
  • Gluttony: 6/10
    • What is this guy? But doing something others hate the most was the most classic villain thing he did.
    • This guy made Re:Zero interesting and entertaining til season 4 so he should be rewarded based on that.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 17
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler, and not only about this episode.

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 17 twice.

The episode finally started the loop where Subaru would overcome the obstacles. The first thing Subaru did was go meet Emilia. She was so happy, and she kicked what's-his-name, who quickly fled from her. Wait, why did he escape that fast while in the other loops Subaru couldn't make him leave and had to fight him for a long time? Then Subaru met Beatrice and Ram and they talked about the tactics there. Emilia's actions were also so cute, especially when she pressed her cheek against Beatrice's.

Next, Subaru went to a place with Shaula, Meili, and Foxidna. I thought he would prevent Shaula from becoming the scorpion, but he couldn't prevent it. But instead, Emilia kicked the scorpion and made it fall to the ground from the tower, but that scorpion climbed up quickly to the balcony again. I wondered what the strategy was, but somehow, Subaru, Meili, and Beatrice would deal with the scorpion by riding the mabeast like a centaur while Meili was controlling it. And they climbed down from the tower and of course the scorpion followed Subaru. I was like, wait, was it okay to leave the tower, but Shaula had already become the scorpion so it didn't matter. But I still didn't know his strategy.

On the other side, Roy climbed upstairs while he couldn't reach out to Rui and Ley, but he didn't care about it. He was totally okay with being alone and fighting against Subaru and others, well, maybe because he thought he was strong enough? Then Ram was waiting for him. Of course, Subaru or Ram was the one who would fight and defeat Gluttony, thinking about Rem and the entire story in Re:Zero so far.

Then, Julius fought against Reid. I wondered how Julius got to where Reid was. In this loop, Subaru didn't tell him to go battle against Reid, if I remember correctly. Maybe he found Roy while moving around? Emilia also went there, but Reid didn't remember her, so Roy's authority affected Reid too. I thought in the first loop where she was forgotten, Reid might've remembered her, but I was wrong. Anyway, then because she passed the exam, she kept climbing up the tower, and that was Subaru's biggest bet in this loop, I think. Julius was fighting against Reid alone while Foxidna was just watching him. I guessed he was going to get his spirits' power back, but I expected he would do so after they defeated Gluttony. So, he just re-contracted with them right then and got his power back. The reason he could do it now, when he couldn't in the previous loops, was probably that Foxidna was there — she passed on what Subaru wanted her to tell him — and also his conversation with Reid. The fight animation between them started with free-moving camera angles, and it sometimes felt slow or even stopped, but it still showed how fast and intense the battle was. But I still imagined he couldn't defeat the Sword Saint, but the ending was kinda good and logical. The last blow seemed to kill Julius but it didn't, fortunately. That's why Julius admitted, at that moment, that Reid had won the battle. Also, Anastasia was back in that scene. Foxidna had known all along why she was hiding, but she reached out to Anastasia so she could watch Julius at the top of his game. The reason why she hid was she couldn't bear losing her memories of Julius. Well, had she really never lost anything important in her life before? Anyway, right before she forgot him, she shouted his name while he was fighting against Reid at the last blow. Then they introduced themselves to each other because he knew she had forgotten him.

I think what Subaru bet was if Emilia could pass all the tower's exams, Shaula would get back from the scorpion. That's the one thing he needed to clear, and there may not have been any other solution. That was why Emilia was the key. In the next episode, because the title is "Ram", the story will mainly be about Ram vs. Gluttony, I guess. But I don't think it will end there, because defeating this Sin Archbishop would probably be the last of this arc so before that, Emilia would solve Shaula's curse, and Shaula's problem would end?

Scores

  • Emilia: 9/10
    • In this episode, she was so happy and pressing her cheek against Beatrice's was also cute
  • Julius: 8/10
    • He was a commoner but tried to behave the way he wanted to be. The more episodes go by, the more I like him

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 16
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler, and not only about this episode.

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 16 twice.

So, this episode was pretty simple. Subaru saw his past memories from when he came to Lugunica onward, and then met himself in the Corridor of Memories. Because he had already died 15 times in the tower, it made sense that he thought the original Subaru had something special that other isekai protagonists would have in their isekai world. But he was disappointed that the original Subaru didn't. And he watched those dozens of return-by-death memories one after another, and it hit him hard. Of course, it would drive anyone insane if you could feel the pain and watch the memories.

The scene between Subaru and the other Subaru was great. Up to this episode, the Subaru in the tower was, actually, literally "Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World," because he didn't remember a thing. And even so, he cared about everyone and thanked everyone. It was a great scene — he thought he would disappear, and he still showed his appreciation. He also thought only the original Subaru could overcome the situation, because he had already failed 15 times and relied upon his assumption that the original Subaru had a special power. Also, it was great that they argued about who Rem belonged to, even if it sounded weird. But Rem said so herself, that she was Subaru's, so he took her at her word; still, it was kinda funny that neither of them would let the other Subaru have her. The voice actor of Subaru was also good. In most of his lines, when the original Subaru spoke, his voice sounded mature and strong, while the other Subaru's voice sounded like a kid when he was calm, or just angry when he got pissed off.

And he finally got back to his original self with his memories. It turned out Gluttony, Rui Arneb, got back from the other Subaru. So, the other Subaru moved around with his own memories, but once he disappeared in the Corridor of Memories, it was back to Rui. And that had been the plan from the beginning — how they were going to get the memories and authority of Subaru. However, she didn't want to take Subaru's experiences of death, and didn't want to share them with her other self. Her other self thought she was monopolizing it for some reason and they started fighting each other. Well, I guess they'll kill each other rather than share these memories, and both end up dead? Anyhow, Subaru knew the essence of Gluttony, who wouldn't accept anything painful or unpleasant, and always wanted to get something good or pleasant from others. He didn't even have any hard feelings toward her, though, despite what she did to him.

Anyhow, then the next episode will be at the tower and they'll start fighting the enemies one by one. It seems Emilia's memory had already been lost, so it was actually the right move to fight at the tower instead of trying to save it.

Scores

  • Episode: 8/10
  • Subaru: 9/10
    • I liked that he's a guy without any special power. Well, technically, he definitely has something, but it's not as powerful as what others have.
    • I liked the scene where the two Subarus talk.
  • Rui: 5/10
    • Is this the last time we'll see this Gluttony? Anyway, she was a person who just trapped Subaru and ended up killing herself.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 8

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 8 twice.

Because of that, Roxy wasn't allowed in. I guess she headed back by road on her own afterward because nobody was with her, and she knew it could take days. The reason why Rudy took time to be teleported was... Man God? Or the capacity of the magic? The teleport magic's animation reminded me of the background when Rudy met Man God.

Rudy also avoided answering, when he and Sylphie were asked, whether he knew Man God or not. She answered she didn't know, and I wondered whether she had just lied. Obviously, he lied because he had been attacked by Orsted the last time he answered that he knew. And they didn't have a way to recognize it. But I guess she didn't have such an experience, so she answered honestly. And in that case, why were they detected? Because of their magic capacity? Or magic without an incantation was detected, and they thought that was the handiwork of Man God, though Rudy figured it out by himself and taught her? Or, Rudy was actually created by Man God?

Anyhow, the flying fortress was a huge castle with nature inside it, and then they entered the throne room and met Perugius. He was intimidating, and many people were nervous, but Nanahoshi was calm and didn't hesitate to push back at him. Perugius was definitely a good guy. He also reacted to a couple of things: one was the fully autonomous doll, and the other was Rudy and Sylphie. I didn't know the intent behind naming their son if they had one, but did he have some intentions to bring Rudy and Sylphie onto his side? But why only a son? Zanoba's fully autonomous doll was rare even for him, so probably that fortress wasn't really industrialized. He also didn't know about the displacement incident. He thought it wasn't by humans, but was it really? I thought someone like Man God did it.

Also, we finally got to know why Elinalise got her curse. She was found in a labyrinth without her memory and emotions, and got emotions afterward, but never got her memories back. Even though she was married, her husband was killed and she needed to deal with her curse. And she needed to leave the elf village that had taken her in, because of her curse. Rudy empathized with her even though she hid her past, and this reminded me what a good character Rudy was. Rudy's past life was not going well.

Anyhow, then they talked about taking a lecture on teleport magic from Nanahoshi's master. And at lunch, they ate food similar to Japanese food. Because Nanahoshi really wanted to go back to her world, she shed tears while eating it, and I empathized with her. Then Cliff and Zanoba found a path to the underground, and some murals. But what were they? The Armored Dragon King immediately came and kicked them out. Did they mean something? He didn't say so, but were they murals from Laplace's time or something?

Also, Rudy was advised not to use his magic in the fortress. But Sylphie, who uses the same kind of magic as him, used hers when Nanahoshi came to their room because she was coughing a lot. Sylphie felt a little weird when she used her magic and tried to use more. But then Nanahoshi threw up blood. I didn't know it was because of her magic, or it was because of Nanahoshi's health, but probably the former. That place wasn't a good place to use magic for Sylphie or Rudy.

So, in the next episode, something will start happening. I want to see what's going to happen. They'll probably save Nanahoshi and come down from the flying fortress.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 15
item.description:

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 15 twice. I didn't see this coming.

What was impressive was that Subaru counted his deaths and kept retrying like 15 times. And there were so many attempts he made, but almost everything was aimed at killing him. And he ended up unable to move his legs out of fear, because after so many attempts, he knew he would die whichever route he tried next.

For example, Reid Astrea. Picking up from the last episode, Julius explained to him that he was the Gluttony, Roy. And then, Julius said that Reid was eaten but took over Roy's body. I was wondering how he had come down during a few of Subaru's return-by-death loops, but now this is explained. As expected, he defeated Subaru and the others easily. There wasn't even a fight scene animated. Afterward Satella came and the tower started falling apart, but even during that, he still moved and fought Julius and Subaru and killed them. He even cut through Satella's magic, probably with Julius's sword. During the tower's collapse, the animation was great because, well, you know it's hard to picture a situation like that in a fantasy world. Also, in one of Subaru's attempts, he was trying to reach Reid and Reid was already with Roy. And then Subaru saw how Reid took over Roy, but it was a scary scene, and Reid was a monster.

In another of Subaru's attempts, he met Shaula. She was always positive and high-spirited, but it hit me that she missed her master a lot and she didn't want Subaru to leave after only a few days. She told them the 4 rules of the trials but there was another secret. And the secret one was not to break an exam, and that was the one Reid actually did and triggered her change into her scorpion form. I feel the drawings and animation for her in this episode were good, and the part where they fell from the balcony was especially well-drawn and beautiful. I'd already seen one cut on YouTube, but I didn't know how they ended up. Anyhow, after watching this episode twice, I thought she was the main heroine of this arc, or at least for this Subaru. She hasn't been saved and she's confined to the tower, so he is going to free her somehow. Come to think of it, who was her master, really? The person who had the witch's curse, too, 400 years ago?

After so many attempts, at the end of this episode, Subaru couldn't move but he could see 2 lights in his authority. I was wondering what they were, but because their colors were the same, it meant they were both Subaru. And he reached the place, and it was the book of Subaru Natsuki in the archive. When I saw that, I thought the archive was perhaps only books taken by Gluttony, but that's very likely not it, because it doesn't explain Meili's case. So, the archive held not only the dead, but also people who had lost their memories.

The next episode is obviously about Subaru's memory. Will he remember his own memories? I bet. Also, his return point itself might move further back, which has never happened before. I don't know what else he could do to overcome this situation — or maybe he will gain another authority, because he got it when he came back from Reid's book.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 14
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler, and not only about this episode.

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 14 twice. I didn't expect that ending.

So, in this episode, I was able to understand a lot of things. First of all, if Subaru, Ram, and Beatrice rushed to Emilia's place, Shaula turned into a scorpion. Why did that happen to her? It was probably a spell her master cast on her in the past, one that would turn her into a mabeast if she went outside of the tower, in order to stop her from abandoning the tower. So I bet while she was protecting the tower on the balcony, something pushed her and she became the mabeast.

For some reason, the souls he could recognize were the ones close to him — Ram, Rem, Patrasche, Shaula, Foxidna, and so on — but he couldn't recognize others like Gluttony, a lot of mabeasts, or Reid. Why did he get this authority now? I have no idea. And he got it right before Shaula's scorpion appeared, and before the witch did. And why did the witch come here? I have no idea. It's probably related to why Shaula fell. And Subaru didn't remember what happened after the witch came, which implied to me that he became the Archbishop again at that time, and died.

Then Gluttony was able to take Emilia's name if they got to her place too late. And also, if they didn't stop Reid, he met up with Gluttony too, and the battle turned into chaos. When it comes to Gluttony, he used a few techniques and he also spoke in a few ways. It was obviously because he ate a lot of people's memories and gained their experience. He didn't share his memories with the Gluttony in the book, though, because he thought Subaru still had his memories. It was funny to see when he was trying to imitate Rem's behavior, honestly. The voice actor did his best with that. It was patently clear that Ram was furious with Gluttony too, because her memories of Rem had been taken by him. His authority showed some weaknesses when Ram lost her memories of Emilia, because her memories no longer added up when she lost her memories of both Rem and Emilia. Then the cliffhanger at the end was that Reid Astrea was one of the Gluttonies. This was the most surprising thing to me in this episode and I even let out a noise at the end on my first watch. I was wondering why he didn't help defeat Gluttony, or why Gluttony came into the tower in the first place, but this made it clear. Also, when I watched it the second time, I noticed he hadn't lost his memories of Emilia, and also Subaru couldn't recognize his soul at all, so I should've been able to figure it out. This episode's subtitle was "Five Obstacles". What are they? At least from what I've seen, there are a few candidates.

  1. Mabeasts from the sand dunes

  3. Shaula's scorpion
  4. The Witch
  5. Reid Astrea
  6. Subaru turning into an Archbishop

And then, I believe another Archbishop who pushed Subaru with Rem's voice was there, too. But this may not count because it's not something Subaru has seen so far and maybe just how the animation was done. I think these have to be overcome in this arc. I think at least, this arc will end the battle against Gluttony, and may solve some of the issues they currently have, like Rem, Julius, and Subaru. item.title: First thoughts after watching Re:Zero Season 4 Episode 13
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler, and not only about this episode.

I watched Re:Zero season 4 episode 13 twice. "That is that, this is this."

I think it made sense how other people like Julius felt toward Subaru. Subaru spoke like he knew Julius pretty well, even though Subaru had said he lost his memory the day before. It sounded like a lie, but he was on his fifth life because of the return by death, and he saw how Julius confronted Reid by himself in a desperate situation. Honestly, if I were Julius, I would think he was lying for some reason, or just a creepy person. But Julius trusted him and believed his words, and also he had his pride as a knight. So he looked like he was convinced by what Subaru said.

Before they reached the archive, Emilia's expressions toward Subaru changed a lot, too. She is the main heroine, so she was given priority in the animation. For example, when he replied to what she said with "that's not something you hear these days", she broke into a big smile. But then, when he thought he should be the one to check Reid's book, she was worried though other people had already made up their minds about the consequences.

Speaking of the conversation in the archive, it was a bit of a long conversation before he opened the book, at least that was what I thought when I watched it the first time. That was... maybe because he was afraid of losing his memories again, and also he cared about the others who were worried about him, like Emilia and Beako.

And I was wondering how the tower got overrun by monsters in Subaru's previous lives, but now we have an idea, thanks to this episode. Gluttony — the big brothers — invaded the tower successfully. Maybe partially because Shaula was with Subaru and she didn't notice them sooner. And the reason why they were able to attack so early was... what? We know that there are multiple Gluttonies, and it looked like they shared their memories, because they all had Rem's memories. So I guess they shared memories, and when the Gluttony sister in the Corridor of Memories ate Subaru's memory, they knew where Subaru and the others were, too? Shaula's protective magic for the tower, Infinite Hell Snipe, also had a very long and wide range, but it wasn't enough to exterminate all the mabeasts, so plenty of them got inside.

In terms of Subaru and Gluttony in the Corridor of Memories, from their conversation, I felt that was the plot the author wanted to write. Subaru used to return by death a lot, but he never lost his memory, or died completely. So it was an agonizing moment: he wanted to protect himself, while Gluttony was trying to trap him into strangling her and splitting him apart. She wanted to be dead. This was my understanding from what she said. Well, Subaru agonized throughout this series MANY times so this was the Nth time for us to watch this kind of scene.

One thing I didn't understand was why Gluttony couldn't see or notice Rem. Apparently, she showed up because Gluttony had to pull her memories out and throw them away in order to eat Subaru's memory — her memory of him stopped them from doing so. But does that mean they can't perceive anything they throw away? Or maybe, this is another thing only Subaru can do, like his Witch's curse.

By the way, I knew Rem was in this episode because I'd seen a spoiler, but I wouldn't have expected her if I hadn't known it. I had forgotten but she was strict with Subaru, so I didn't expect her to speak so harshly when they met. But she saw him as a hero and never wavered on that. What was the effect Subaru received before she disappeared? After that, he became positive and optimistic. Did his memory come back at that point, or did it remind him of Emilia or other people in the tower in his previous lives? Also, her memory orb was lost in the corridor, so does that mean her memories are completely lost? Or do the other Gluttonies still have her memories, so they could be recovered? Maybe that's the case, and she will not remember what happened there because that memory didn't exist in the other Gluttonies' memories. Subaru thought he could meet her again. In the worst case, considering that the Corridor of Memories is the place to "filter" souls, maybe she was "filtered" this time. Well, but in this series, nobody has died for good, right? So that seems very unlikely.

And we know a little about Gluttony now. It's weird that she could split into two, but at least that's an ability she has. And because there is a book that leads to the Corridor of Memories, I feel in season 4, they will defeat Gluttony. I also saw another spoiler that Emilia will be forgotten, so defeating them and recovering the memories will be important, too. Besides, I think Julius will defeat Reid to get his spirits back. So I think that will be the next episode.

Scores

  • Episode: 8/10
  • Subaru: 7/10
    • He believed what Gluttony said too easily, even though he knew she had eaten his memories. But at the same time, this was a mysterious world so I can empathize with him worrying that he might disappear.
    • He often agonized and showed an unsightly side of himself, like trying to work out from others how he should behave.
  • Julius: 8/10
    • He is cool and straightforward. He trusted Subaru a lot, maybe because he took a liking to him at first sight.
  • Rem: 9/10
    • It's been a while since we've seen her in the series. For that alone, it should be worth 10/10 honestly.
    • This time, she was the person who pointed Subaru in the right direction, again. What a dedicated person. She believed him too much, but she might have found out he can return by death at that time.
    • Her cool voice and her caring words for Subaru are good.
  • Gluttony: 6/10
    • They're disgusting characters but now this character is a good villain. We now know their motivation is to become happy and for that, they steal other people's happy memories.
    • Their words sometimes hit on the truth, too.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 2

She even tried to find and meet Rudeus because she didn't want to admit he was real, or because she somehow thought she could've beaten him. But after seeing him, it looked like she changed her mind, and her opinion of Eris changed a little. Probably because he was so exceptional and she couldn't imagine even Eris catching up with him. At the training hall, when the Water God came, they were on their guard against Eris the moment she walked in. I thought it meant Eris was so strong compared to them. Then Eris fought the Water King and lost, but Nina beat her, so their strengths formed a triangle. And after they went over the improvements the Water King suggested, Nina started looking after Eris more. It was partially because Eris also started talking to her more, I guess. And until then, Eris only cared about Orsted and she didn't think about others, except for Rudeus, and even that was infrequent.

So, a few months or years later, in the next training session with the Water King, Eris had changed after getting advice from Nina. She was clean, she didn't rush straight into attacking the Water King, so we were able to see how different she had become in an instant. And when Eris smiled at the Water King, the Water King let her guard down, and Eris landed a hit. And I also forgot a lot because it was in season 1, but Eris was a girl who was very emotional and showed her emotions on her face, not only hostility or desperation toward someone. By the way, I didn't remember Eris was able to use fire magic. Or she just didn't have to use it until this episode? I don't remember.

The action in this episode was also good. The fights between the Water King, Eris and Nina weren't that good, but the action in the fights against the beasts moved pretty well with a fast pace and dynamic camera angles. We could feel the speed and momentum as well as the power when Eris broke the ice cliff. During the training against the Water King, Eris's sword also looked different from the others', and it used the same effect as when she took down the North Emperor, which was unique and indicated she did something different.

Nina saw Rudeus at the best worst time, and she didn't even understand what happened. Well, I also didn't remember what happened at that time, but Rudeus somehow got attention for a duel. Then she only saw the last moment, when he hit Badigadi with his magic and the demon king was blown away. She probably didn't understand it was a deal where the demon king wouldn't dodge and would just take a hit from his strongest magic, so he had as much time as he wanted to cast it. Maybe that left her with an impression of him as a much stronger character than he actually was.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 12
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 12. And this was the last episode of season 1. This episode was 6/10, and the entire season was 8/10. This was a great romance anime. This episode covered a few events for Maki and Umi before closing the season, and also showed there might be a next season.

The last episode ended at the beginning of the year, but this episode showed Valentine's Day, White Day, and Umi's birthday. On Valentine's Day, what I thought was that Maki's cooking skill was actually good, so how could she give him a chocolate he would be satisfied with? And in this episode, it was revealed that Umi's cooking skill was not good, or at least she didn't cook often. So she tried to cook something difficult and challenging from the beginning, and failed to do it. I thought Maki should help her make the chocolate together, and he did it so I was kinda satisfied with this small touch.

Then, on White Day, Maki returned something to others. Somehow, there were meanings for gifts and Maki tried to give snacks to each person matching the meaning. For Umi, it was a lot of candy, in both color and amount, instead of cookies.

On Umi's birthday, Maki gave Umi a hairpin, but it looked expensive for a high school student. But it was a good one and Umi wore it. What was good in that scene was that Amami also noticed Umi showing sides of herself Amami didn't know, so she wondered whether Umi had a boyfriend.

And it was the end of their first year of high school. If there is a second season, then the classes will be reshuffled, so this group will be split up.

Overall, this anime was good. There were not many big events, as you would expect from a model slice-of-life anime, but the episodes made progress slowly and steadily. Also, unlike other romance anime, the relationship between Maki and Umi really progressed enough. Interactions between characters were more natural and not awkward, and the main characters didn't talk in their heads too much. So the story was one of the best among romance anime. Well, one weird thing was they loved sharks a LOT.

Animation was also great. There were not many action scenes, but the background art and its animation, and Umi's eyes, were drawn and animated gorgeously. Sometimes, some characters looked weird to me in the animation, but it was acceptable.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 23 (season 2, episode 11)
item.description:
This post includes a spoiler.

I watched Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 23 twice. 9/10. Story was 5/5, animation was 5/5, voices and audio were 4/5. This was a great episode. The main thing was the battle between Zeo and Elfie.

This episode showed how fierce the battle was between two Magia Vanders. And obviously, Ellenor lost to Elfie with ice magic alone, so they both seemed strong. So, the battle was basically one between the cream of the crop and it was worth watching. Zeo's attacks were mostly simple. He used his lightning to move blazing fast, but that was so fast that the animation got good. Like when he threw the wand and then he instantly reached the place where the wand landed, or when the wand came and broke Elfie's clone from an unexpected angle.

Elfie's magic was the exact opposite. She built an ice castle, made a lot of clones, attacked with hundreds of ice shards from every angle, and summoned more ice by drawing a large magic circle. And also, using those remnants, she completely froze his lightning with her ice magic. What was unexpected was that she punched him, with a perfect, anime-style motion, unlike what I imagine a mage would do, and with her magic, the blow landed on him completely. Also, before starting the incantation of her prime magic, she sat on the handrail of the staircase and slid down, and that was so weird. It probably showed her princess-ish behavior but not something you do during a fight.

The animation itself was also great. It wasn't the kind of episode that stops to talk. Characters, buildings, and objects move a lot and fast in most scenes. Of course, when they talked about something, it stopped, but that made a good contrast with the fast-moving scenes. And the entire episode was for this battle alone, and it didn't even end within the episode. The battle between Will and Devander was more like a showcase of Will's Wis ability, so there was some of that, but not at this level. So I was satisfied with this episode.

Story-wise, Elfie put all her effort into fighting him for Will. It was because she had only waited for Will all along, and it was Elfie's turn to do something. This was great, because I thought she hadn't really done much so far and they already had a relationship. Well, it was still a question why they did, but at least, the fact that she stepped up to fight Zeo with all her might changed my opinion about her in this episode. Colette got angry, though. I guess she's already completely lost her chance.

It was also great how Carriot and Ellenor thought and saw the battle. They knew who those two were, so they didn't stop them. And they also noticed that even Zeo got serious once they both used their prime magic. Finn was also smiling and watching the battle, and somehow he knew everything, including Elfie's secret magic. I wonder why he knew how deep Zeo went into the Dungeon, though. He might've been with Zeo? He used to be with the Mage Queen in the past, so I guess he also enjoyed watching mages' battles.

Also, I liked the voice acting of Elfie before the fight started, and Sarissa's shout was great too.

So what's going to happen in the next episode? It looks like Aaron will come down into the venue and butt in. Then Will is going to join Elfie's faction and the season will end shortly.
